title: Vishnu's eye-offering and the gift of the Sudarshana chakra
brief: Vishnu worships Shiva with a thousand lotuses; Shiva hides one and Vishnu offers his own eye — earning the epithet Padmaksha/Kamala-nayana and the Sudarshana discus. Source: Shiva Purana, Kotirudra-samhita ch. 34. Verified: only a one-line *Variant* in divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md line 83; no story treatment. Cross-link divyastras file and the vishnu forms file.

title: Śiva loses to Pārvatī at dice — the dyūta-krīḍā and the Śabarī huntress
brief: The Kedara-khanda close: Shiva gambles away everything to Parvati and stalks off; Vishnu rigs a rematch, and Parvati disguised as a Shabari huntress wins him back — charter of the Uma-Maheshvara dyuta-krida iconography. Source: Skanda Purana, Maheshvara-khanda, Kedara-khanda chs. 34–35. Verified: no Shiva-Parvati dice content anywhere (the only dice hits are Yudhishthira/Kojagari/Draupadi).

title: Brāhmottara-khaṇḍa vrata tales — Sīmantinī, Bhadrāyu's Śiva-kavaca, Mahānandā's rudrākṣa
brief: GROUPED catalog of three gap-list entries from the same khanda: Simantini's Somavara-vrata restoring her drowned husband Citrangada (chs. 8–9), prince Bhadrayu resuscitated with the Shiva-kavaca and tested by Shiva as a tiger (chs. 10–14), and the courtesan Mahananda's rudraksha vow (ch. 20). Source: Skanda Purana, Brahma-khanda, Brahmottara-khanda chs. 8–20. Verified: simantini, bhadrayu, and mahananda-rudraksha all grep to zero corpus-wide; festivals-and-vratas.md mentions Monday vrats storylessly.

title: Daśaratha and Śani — the king who stopped Saturn
brief: Dasharatha rides into the sky to stop Shani transiting Rohini (averting twelve-year famine), pleases Saturn by fearlessness, and receives the Dasharatha-Shani-stotra still recited today. Source: Skanda Purana, Nagara-khanda (Hatakeshvara-kshetra section), the Dasharatha-Shanaishcara chapters. Verified: navagraha.md gives exactly one line; characters/dasharatha.md has none. Cross-link both.

title: Kārtika-māhātmya devotee tales — King Cola vs Viṣṇudāsa, Dharmadatta-Kalahā, Dhaneśvara, Satyabhāmā's former birth
brief: MERGED (Skanda + Padma duplicates — the same tale-cluster recited each Kartika): rich King Cola vs the poor bhakta Vishnudasa who cooks his own flesh; Dharmadatta and the demoness Kalaha freed by Tulasi-water merit; the sinner Dhaneshvara saved by Kartika-dipa; Krishna telling Satyabhama her former birth as Gunavati; the Alakshmi episode. Sources: Skanda Purana, Vaishnava-khanda, Karttikamasa-mahatmya chs. 24–29; Padma Purana, Uttara-khanda 88–117. Verified: vishnudasa/dhaneshvara/kalaha/gunavati all grep to zero; jalandhara-vrinda.md covers only the Tulasi-origin side.

title: Nārada's māyā — the sage becomes Sushīlā, wife of King Tāladhvaja
brief: The famous maya-parable: Narada bathes in a tirtha, becomes the woman Sushila, marries Taladhvaja, bears and loses sons and grandsons, and is restored — a lifetime remembered as moments. Source: Devi Bhagavata Purana VI.28–31. Verified: taladhvaja greps return zero and narada.md (a full character deep-dive) has no maya-transformation episode; write as file or major section in narada.md, distinct from the Shiva Purana Narada-moha item.

title: Śatākṣī / Śākambharī and the slaying of Durgamāsura
brief: Durgama steals the Vedas, drought follows; the hundred-eyed Shatakshi weeps rain, feeds the world from her body as Shakambhari, and slays Durgama — charter for the name 'Durga' and the living Shakambhari cult (Sambhar, Saharanpur, Shakambhari Purnima). Source: Devi Bhagavata Purana VII.28; foretold in Devi Mahatmya 11; Skanda parallel. Verified: only one-line foretelling/etymology mentions in devi-mahatmya-and-the-great-goddess.md and devi-forms-and-navadurga.md.

title: Bhṛgu's curse on Viṣṇu — Kāvyamātā's beheading, Śukra-Jayantī, and Bṛhaspati's impersonation
brief: THREE-WAY MERGE (DBP entry + Matsya Shukra-Jayanti entry + Ramayana Uttara 51 Durvasa-prophecy entry — one story-complex): Shukra's tapas for the mrita-sanjivani counter-lore, Indra's daughter Jayanti's ten-year union, Vishnu beheading Bhrigu's wife who shelters the asuras, Bhrigu's curse dooming Vishnu to repeated mortal births and wife-separation (the karmic charter of the avataras and of Sita's loss), and Brihaspati's impersonation of the asura-guru. Sources: Matsya Purana 47; Devi Bhagavata IV.10–15; Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara-kanda 51. Verified: the-gurus-brihaspati-and-shukra.md names Jayanti in one spouse-line and covers only the Kacha episode; bhrigu.md has only the chest-kick cycle.

title: Ṣaṣṭhī, Maṅgalā Caṇḍī, Svadhā and Dakṣiṇā — the Prakṛti-khaṇḍa goddess aetiologies
brief: FOUR-WAY MERGE (Shashthi + Mangala-Chandi + Brahmavaivarta duplicate + Svadha-Dakshina): the origin tales of the minor Prakriti goddesses — Shashthi reviving King Priyavrata's stillborn son (charter of the sixth-day and Chhathi worship), Mangala Chandi worshipped by Shiva before Tripura (Tuesday/Bengal cult), Svadha given to the Pitris, Dakshina wed to Yajna-purusha. Sources: Devi Bhagavata IX.44–47; Brahmavaivarta Purana, Prakriti-khanda 41–44. Verified: shashthi hits are calendar lines plus the lumped one-liner in brahmavaivarta-purana.md; peer files manasa.md and shitala.md set the convention.

title: Kuvalayāśva (Ṛtadhvaja) and Madālasā — the nāga-world romance
brief: The Markandeya's longest romance: Ritadhvaja slays Patalaketu, rescues Madalasa in Patala, loses her to a false death-report, and the naga king Ashvatara restores her from his own breast — the narrative setup of the already-covered Madalasa Upadesha lullaby. Source: Markandeya Purana, Cantos 20–27 (Pargiter). Verified: only lullaby bullets in 90-literature-corpus/puranas/markandeya-purana.md and two TIMELINE lines; the adventure is untold.

title: Vipaścit in hell — the king who gave his merit to the damned
brief: King Vipashchit, sent briefly to Naraka, finds his presence cools the tortured, refuses Yama's summons to heaven, and transfers his merit to free hell's denizens — a landmark of Hindu compassion-ethics, much cited in karma scholarship. Source: Markandeya Purana, Cantos 13–15 (Pargiter, the hell-visions in the Jada-father dialogue). Verified: vipashchit hits are only Indra-name lists in manvantara files; the afterlife files have no trace.

title: Anasūyā and the halted sunrise — the pativratā's night and the Dattātreya boon
brief: Mandavya's curse dooms the leprous brahmin to die at sunrise; his wife commands the sun never to rise; the gods beg Anasuya, who restores dawn, revives the husband, and earns the boon of the Trimurti as her sons. Source: Markandeya Purana, Cantos 16–17 (Pargiter), prelude to the Dattatreya section. Verified: atri-anasuya.md tells only the nagna-bhiksha version (zero sunrise/mandavya hits); write as new file or major section there.

title: Khāṇḍikya and Keśidhvaja — the Vishnu Purana's concluding yoga dialogue
brief: The VP's coda: the rival Janaka-line cousins — Khandikya master of karma, Keshidhvaja of atma-jnana — reconciled when the deposed Khandikya asks not for his kingdom but for yoga instruction; the discourse Ramanuja quotes. Source: Vishnu Purana VI.5–7 (Wilson Book VI, ch. V–VII). Verified: khandikya/keshidhvaja grep to zero corpus-wide; vishnu-purana.md's Amsha 6 summary omits it.

title: The Kṣupa–Dadhīca dispute — brahma vs kṣatra and the charter of Sthāṇu-tīrtha
brief: King Kshupa (backed by Vishnu) and Dadhicha quarrel over kshatra vs brahma power; the Shiva-hardened sage survives the vajra, defeats the discus, and curses the gods to burn at Daksha's yajna — the Linga Purana's Shaiva-supremacy proof-story tied to Sthaneshvara. Source: Linga Purana, Purva-bhaga chs. 35–36; Shiva/Skanda parallels. Verified: kshupa greps return zero; dadhichi.md tells only the vajra-bone gift — cross-link it.

title: Pārijāta-haraṇa — Krishna's war with Indra for the Pārijāta tree
brief: The Harivamsha's longest late set-piece: Satyabhama's pride, the uprooting of the Parijata, full war with Indra, Aditi's mediation, and Satyabhama's Punyaka-vrata — basis of later kavya and dance (Bhamakalapam). Source: Harivamsha, Vishnu Parva (Dutt) ch. 69 ff.; cf. Vishnu Purana 5.30–31, Bhagavata X.59. Verified: krishna-lila.md now has a one-sentence bullet (X.59) and divine-objects-and-treasures.md one bullet — the Harivamsha war-cycle and Punyaka-vrata remain untold; cross-link both.

title: Viṣṇudharmottara Purāṇa — text profile
brief: Profile of the encyclopedic upapurana: Markandeya teaching King Vajra (last Yadava), Khanda 1's legend-cycles, Khanda 2's rajadharma/sciences, Khanda 3's Chitrasutra (earliest Indian painting treatise, with the origin-of-painting legend of Narayana drawing Urvashi in mango juice). Source: Vishnudharmottara Purana, 3 khandas (Priyabala Shah trans.; Kramrisch, Part III). Verified: only two one-liners in upapuranas-overview.md; the puranas directory profiles all mahapuranas plus other upapuranas but not this; the Urvashi legend is absent corpus-wide.

title: Prajāpati and his daughter — Rudra the avenger and the deer's head
brief: The Brahmanas' central transgression-myth: Prajapati pursues his daughter as a stag; the gods compound their dread forms into Bhutavat/Rudra who pierces him — Prajapati becomes Mrigashiras, the arrow Ardra, the seed a lake whence creatures arise. Sources: Aitareya Brahmana 3.33–34; Shatapatha 1.7.4.1–8; Maitrayani Samhita 4.2.12; cf. RV 10.61.5–7. Verified: only Puranic descendants (Brahma-Shatarupa; Bhairava fifth head) and a one-line allusion in nakshatras.md exist; the Vedic story is untold. Cross-link nakshatras.md and shiva-myth-cycle.md.

title: Indra and Namuci — the wager, the surā, and the foam weapon
brief: The pact 'neither by day nor night, neither wet nor dry,' the beheading with water-foam at twilight, and the severed head rolling after Indra crying 'friend-betrayer' — with rich Samhita/Brahmana variants and the Mahabharata retelling. Sources: Shatapatha 12.7.3.1–4; Taittiriya Brahmana 1.7.1.6–8; RV 8.14.13; Mbh Shalya 9.43. Verified: only the one-line foam-trick parenthesis in indra.md line 71 and roster mentions in asura-wars-and-roster.md.

title: The Aśvins and their rescue-deeds cycle
brief: A deity file for the twin gods — absent from the deities section — anchored on the deed-catalogue: Bhujyu saved from the shipwreck, Vishpala's iron leg, Rebha and Vandana from the wells, Ghosha cured and wed, Atri from the burning pit; note their Cyavana and Dadhyanc deeds already live in other files. Sources: Rigveda 1.116–118, 1.112, 10.39–40. Verified: vishpala/rebha grep to zero; Bhujyu has one clause in vedic-deities-and-suktas.md line 29.

title: Vāc and the purchase of Soma — why women love song and dance
brief: The somakrayana etiology: the gods turn Vac into a woman to buy Soma from the woman-coveting gandharvas, then win her back when she chooses song and dance over Veda-recitation. Sources: Shatapatha Brahmana 3.2.4.1–7; Taittiriya Samhita 6.1.6.5–6; Aitareya Brahmana 1.27. Verified: gandharvas-and-kinnaras.md covers Soma-guardianship generically but not this tale; saraswati.md treats Vac only theologically.

title: Trita Āptya — the sage in the well and the scapegoat of the gods
brief: Trita thrown into the well by Ekata and Dvita, praying his way out, and the Aptyas' Brahmana office as wipers-away of the gods' blood-guilt — the classic Vedic scapegoat and Avestan Thraetaona cognate. Sources: Rigveda 1.105; Shatapatha 1.2.3.1–5; Jaiminiya Brahmana 1.184. Verified: the only Trita hit is a son-list in manvantara-06-chakshusha.md; Aptya returns zero files.

title: Brāhmaṇa legends catalog — ten Vedic prose tales
brief: GROUPED catalog replacing ten P3 gap entries, all verified zero corpus-wide: Atri and Svarbhanu (RV 5.40; Panchavimsha 4.5.2 — ancestor of the Rahu myth), Dirghajihvi the soma-licker (Jaiminiya 1.161–163), Kavasha Ailusha and the Sarasvati (Aitareya 2.19), Nabhanedishtha (Aitareya 5.14), Vrisha Jana and Tryaruna (Panchavimsha 13.3.12; Brhaddevata 5.14–23), Indra and the Yatis/salavrikas (Aitareya 7.28), the Gaupayanas recalling Subandhu's soul (RV 10.57–60; Brhaddevata 7.83–102), Keshin Darbhya and the ghost Kaupayeya (Jaiminiya 2.269–272), Manu's bull and Kilata-Akuli (Shatapatha 1.1.4.14–17), and Kutsa Aurava the doppelganger (Jaiminiya 3.199–200). Cross-link the brahmana text-profiles in 90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/ (note: shatapatha-brahmana.md already tells Videgha Mathava — model its §5a treatment).

title: Udayana and Vāsavadattā — the Vatsa king's romance cycle
brief: The proverbial romance (Meghaduta's 'elders full of Udayana tales'): capture via the artificial elephant, the lute-teaching, the elopement from Ujjayini, Yaugandharayana's fire-ruse and the Padmavati marriage — parent of Bhasa's Svapnavasavadatta and Harsha's Ratnavali. Source: Kathasaritsagara, Lambhakas II–III (Tarangas 9–19). Verified: all corpus Udayana hits are the Nyaya philosopher or an Ayyappa bandit; vasavadatta/yaugandharayana grep to zero.

title: Siṃhāsana Dvātriṃśikā — the 32 tales of Vikramaditya's throne
brief: Bhoja unearths Vikramaditya's throne and its 32 apsara statuettes each tell a tale of Vikrama's generosity before letting him ascend — core of the pan-Indian Vikramaditya legend, with the Shalivahana rivalry and Bhartrihari fruit-tale attached. Source: Simhasanadvatrimshika (Vikramacharita), ed. Edgerton (HOS 26–27); Hindi Singhasan Battisi. Verified: only a source-tag line and Vikramaditya/Bhartrihari paragraphs in ujjain-avantika.md §IX (which should be cross-linked); no statuette-tale is told.

title: Famous tales of the Kathasaritsagara — Upakoshā, Devasmitā, Lohajaṅgha, Śaktivega's City of Gold
brief: Catalog of the celebrated stand-alone tales: Upakosha shaming her four suitors (I.4), Lohajangha posing as Vishnu at Mathura (II.12), Devasmita and the fidelity-lotus (II.13), Shaktivega and golden Kanakapuri (V), Kalingasena-Somaprabha and the automata (VI). Source: Kathasaritsagara, lambhaka/taranga as listed. Verified: upakosha/devasmita/lohajangha/shaktivega/kalingasena all grep to zero — not even one-line mentions.

title: Hitopadesha — Narayana's book of good counsel
brief: Text profile of the Bengal Panchatantra-reworking: King Sudarshana of Pataliputra's sons taught in four books (Mitralabha, Suhridbheda, Vigraha, Sandhi), with the famous Viravara loyalty-tale; historically among the most-read Sanskrit texts. Source: Hitopadesha of Narayana Pandit (c. 800–1373 CE window). Verified: hitopadesha greps return zero anywhere in the corpus.

title: The Story of Queen Līlā — the two universes in the mind
brief: The Yoga Vasishtha's flagship idealism parable: Lila, granted vision by Sarasvati, travels between nested dream-universes where her dead husband reigns — worlds as mind-appearance. Source: Yoga Vasishtha, Utpatti Prakarana III, chs. ~15–58 (Lila-upakhyana). Verified: zero hits; keep standalone beside the yoga-vasishtha-tales-catalog item, cross-linking it.

title: Siruthondar — the child-curry test of Bhairava
brief: Shiva as a Bhairava ascetic demands a curry of the devotee's only son Seeralan; the parents comply, the guest demands the boy join the meal, and the child runs in alive — the most debated bhakti-extremism tale of Tamil Shaivism, its hero identified with Paranjothi, the Pallava general who sacked Vatapi (642 CE). Source: Periya Puranam, Ciruttondar Nayanar Puranam (no. 36); Sundarar, Tiruttondattokai v. 6. Verified: siruthondar/seeralan grep to zero.

title: Chandesvara — the boy who axed his father's foot
brief: Vicharasharman worships sand-lingas with the herd's milk; his father kicks the linga, the boy severs the leg, and Shiva appoints him Chandesvara, eternal steward of Shiva's property — grounding the Chandikeshvara sub-shrine and clapping custom of every Chola-era Shiva temple. Source: Periya Puranam, Candesvara Nayanar Puranam (no. 20); Agamic adhikara-nandi role. Verified: chandesvara/vicharasharman grep to zero despite the corpus's many Tamil temple files.

title: Alvar hagiographies — the Guruparampara legends
brief: Umbrella hagiography file: the Mudal Alvars pressed together in the storm-corridor at Tirukkovilur sensing Vishnu as the fourth; Tirumazhisai's 'Kanikannan poga' (Vishnu rolling up his serpent-bed); Tiruppan carried into Srirangam on Loka Saranga's shoulders and merging into Ranganatha; Kulasekhara's snake-pot; Periyalvar's Tiruppallandu on Garuda. Sources: Guruparampara Prabhavam 6000-padi; Divya Suri Charitam of Garudavahana Pandita. Verified: kanikannan and loka-saranga grep to zero; the roster file alvars-and-nayanars.md gives one bullet per saint.

title: Tirumangai Alvar — the robber-saint Parakala
brief: Kaliyan turns highway robber to feed devotees, waylays a wedding party that is Vishnu-Lakshmi in disguise, cannot lift the Lord's toe-ring, receives the Ashtakshara from the bridegroom's lips (Tirumanankollai), and later funds Srirangam's third wall with the Nagapattinam golden Buddha. Sources: Guruparampara Prabhavam and Divya Suri Charitam, Parakala chapters; Periya Tirumozhi 1.1. Verified: all Tirumangai hits are geographic one-liners; kumudavalli/tirumanankollai grep to zero. Corpus convention (andal.md, nammalvar.md) supports the file.

title: Nandanar (Tirunālaippōvār) — the full legend
brief: The Pulaiyar bonded labourer ('I will go tomorrow'): Shiva commands Nandi at Tirupunkur to shift aside; the forty-veli field ploughed overnight; the fire-ordeal at Chidambaram and merger with Nataraja — famous far beyond the Periya Puranam through Gopalakrishna Bharati's Nandanar Charitram (1861) and central to caste-and-bhakti debates. Source: Periya Puranam, Tirunalaippovar Nayanar Puranam (no. 18). Verified: only a one-bullet roster entry in alvars-and-nayanars.md line 48; tirupunkur greps return zero.

title: Arunagirinathar — the gopuram leap and the Tiruppugazh
brief: The dissolute youth's suicide-leap from the Tiruvannamalai gopuram caught by Murugan, who writes 'Muttai taru' on his tongue with the Vel; the contest with Sambandandan; the parrot-body errand for the Parijata and the blind king — why his Tiruvannamalai icon is a parrot. Source: Arunagirinathar hagiographic tradition (15th c.) attached to the Tiruppugazh corpus, Kandar Anubhuti, Kandar Alankaram. Verified: coverage is one works-bullet in arupadai-veedu-murugan.md line 12; arunachala-tiruvannamalai-fire-hill.md never names him — cross-link both.

title: Swasthani Brata Katha — the Goma Brahmani cycle (Nepal)
brief: Nepal's most recited narrative text: the month-long Magh recitation frame, Shiva-Sati/Parvati chapters, and the Goma Brahmani story — married by curse to seventy-year-old Shiva Sharma, abandoned, her son Navaraj made king, all resolved by the Svasthani vrata. Source: Svasthani Vrata Katha (oldest MS 1573 CE; framed as Skanda Purana, Kedara Khanda), 31 chapters. Verified: swasthani/goma greps return zero; Nepali tradition otherwise appears only via one Bhanubhakta line.

title: Kanchi-Kaveri — Jagannatha and Balabhadra ride to war
brief: Purushottama Deva, mocked as a 'sweeper' for chhera pahanra, marches on Kanchi; Jagannatha and Balabhadra ride ahead as soldiers on black and white horses and buy curds from the milkmaid Manika with a gold ring; the king weds Padmavati 'to a sweeper' at the festival. Sources: Madala Panji chronicle; Purushottama Dasa's Odia kavya Kanchi-Kaveri (16th c.); reign of Purushottama Deva (1467–97). Verified: kanchi-kaveri greps return zero; the Puri file covers only the Indradyumna cycle.

title: Bhaktas of Jagannatha — Salabega, Dasia Bauri, Bandhu Mohanty
brief: The classic Odia devotee-miracle triad: the Muslim poet Salabega for whom the Ratha halts at his samadhi; Dasia Bauri's coconut accepted by the Lord's own hand; Bandhu Mohanty fed at night with mahaprasada. Source: Odia bhakta tradition — Salabega's bhajans ('Ahe Nila Shaila', early 17th c.), Dasia Bauri and Bandhu Mohanty legends in the bhakta-caritra/Madala Panji lore. Verified: all three grep to zero; comparable bhakta files (ravidas.md) set the convention. Cross-link jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md and ratha-yatra coverage.

title: Annadamangal — Ishwari Patuni and the Vidya-Sundara romance
brief: Bharatchandra Ray's 1752 climax of the mangal-kavya genre: Annada ferried by Ishwari Patuni whose boon 'may my children have milk and rice' is proverbial across Bengal; the Vidya-Sundara tunnel-romance with Sundara saved by Kali; the Bhavananda–Man Singh frame. Source: Annadamangal of Bharatchandra Ray 'Gunakar' (Nadia court), three parts. Verified: annadamangal/bharatchandra/vidya-sundara grep to zero; even regional-and-oral-epics.md omits this fourth major mangal-kavya.

title: Gopichandra and Queen Maynamati — the Nath renouncer-king epic
brief: The great Bengali Nath oral epic: the yogini-queen Maynamati, taught by Gorakshanath, foresees her son King Gopichandra's death unless he renounces; his resistance, the ordeals of Aduna-Paduna, initiation by Hadipa, and return — sung from Bengal to Punjab. Source: Gopichandrer Gan / Manikchandra Rajar Gan (Grierson 1878 Rangpur text; D.C. Sen ed. 1922–24). Verified: gopichandra/maynamati/manikchandra grep to zero; corpus Gorakhnath hits are yoga/Gugga only.

title: Tejaji (Veer Teja) — the Jat serpent-hero who kept his word
brief: Teja of Kharnal promises a serpent to return for its bite, first rescues Lachha Gujari's cows from raiders, returns mutilated and offers his tongue for the fangs — deified as the snakebite-curing god of the Jats (Teja Dashami fairs at Kharnal/Parbatsar/Sursura). Source: Tejaji gatha (Rajasthani bhopa ballad cycle of the Teja shrines). Verified: tejaji greps return zero; the parallel snake-hero Gogaji has a full file.

title: Katamaraju Katha — the Telugu cattle-war epic of Nellore
brief: The second great Telugu oral epic beside Palnadu: the Yadava chief Katamaraju's grazing-rights feud with Nallasiddhi of Nellore, the broken cattle-tribute pact, and the battle of Panchalingala Konda — sung by Golla bards, reckoned the longest Telugu ballad cycle. Source: Katamaraju Kathalu, ed. T.V. Subba Rao (A.P. Sahitya Akademi 1976–78); Blackburn et al., Oral Epics of India (1989). Verified: zero hits; the catalog file's Telugu section has only Palnadu — write as a section there or standalone.

title: Kathivanur Veeran — the martyr-hero theyyam of North Malabar
brief: Mandappan Chekavar of Kathivanur, driven from home, prospers in Coorg, marries Chemmarathi, and falls against Kodagu raiders returning for a forgotten betel pouch; his wife curses and joins his pyre and both are deified — the kolam re-enacts his combat annually. Source: Kathivanur Veeran thottam-pattu (Kannur theyyam liturgy); K.K.N. Kurup, The Cult of Teyyam. Verified: zero hits; peer file muthappan.md sets the convention.

title: Pottan Theyyam — Shiva as the Pulaya who rebukes Shankaracharya
brief: Kerala's anti-caste charter myth: Shiva as a drunken Pulaya corpse-bearer blocks Shankaracharya's path and demolishes caste-purity claims in the thottam dialogue ('if you are cut, do you not bleed as I do?') before revealing himself; performed on live embers. Source: Pottan Theyyam thottam-pattu (Pulappottan samvada), North Malabar kavu tradition. Verified: only the parenthetical one-liner at regional-temple-festivals.md line 41.

title: Icakki Amman Katai (Nili Katai) — the vengeance of Palayanur Nili
brief: The most celebrated Tamil folk revenge-goddess epic: the murdered Nili reborn as a demoness takes the guise of her killer's new wife at Palayanur; when the seventy Velala elders stand surety she kills him, and the seventy immolate themselves to keep their word — proverbial in Tamil and charter of the Icakki Amman vil-pattu cult. Source: Icakkiyamman Katai / Nili Katai (Kanyakumari bow-song tradition; the legend already alluded to in the Periya Puranam ambit). Verified: icakki/nili/palayanur grep to zero.

title: Vadakkan Pattukal — the Northern Ballads of Malabar
brief: The Malayalam heroic-ballad corpus: the Puthooram cycle (Aromal Chekavar betrayed by Chandu at the ankam, warrior-sister Unniyarcha, Aromalunni's revenge) and the Thacholi cycle (Othenan, devotee of Lokanarkavu Bhagavathy) — household-name heroes with shrine/theyyam veneration. Source: Vadakkan Pattukal; C. Achyuta Menon, Ballads of North Malabar (1935). Verified: othenan/unniyarcha/aromal/thacholi grep to zero; the catalog file has no Kerala-ballad section.

title: Panjurli and Guliga — the boar-daiva and the fierce watcher of Tulu Bhūta-Kola
brief: The archetypal Tulu daiva origin-paddanas (globally famous since Kantara): the boar-spirit Panjurli raised in Shiva's household and exiled to protect fields, paired with the wrath-born Guliga; fold in the minor daivas Bobbariya and Kordabbu. Source: Panjurli and Guliga paddanas (Tulu Bhuta-Kola liturgies); Peter J. Claus's paddana studies; Oral Epics of India (1989). Verified: panjurli/guliga grep to zero; the Tulu section of regional-and-oral-epics.md covers only Siri and Koti-Chennaya.

title: Jyotiba (Kedarling) of Wadi Ratnagiri — demon-slayer guardian of Kolhapur
brief: The combined Brahma-Vishnu-Shiva(-Jamadagni) amsha born to sage Pougand who slays Kolhasura, Ratnasura and Raktabhoja to free Karavira — male counterpart of the Kolhapur Mahalakshmi charter, with the pink-gulal Chaitra yatra. Source: Jyotiba/Kedarling sthala tradition (Kedara Vijaya / Karavira Mahatmya cycle). Verified: jyotiba/kolhasura grep to zero; cross-link kolhapur-mahalakshmi-karavira.md and khandoba-martanda-bhairava.md.

title: Tiruvarur Thyagaraja — Manu Needhi Chola and Muchukunda's Somaskanda
brief: The two legends of the supreme Chola kshetra: Manu Needhi Chola driving his chariot over his own son for the cow that rang his justice-bell, and Muchukunda winning the Somaskanda image from Indra with the seven decoy Vitanka shrines and the ajapa-natanam dance. Sources: Tyagaraja/Kamalalaya-kshetra-mahatmya (Skanda tradition); Periya Puranam, Tirumalai-charukkam; Tevaram hymns. Verified: manu-needhi greps return zero; Tiruvarur appears only in a padikasu list-line of 275-paadal-petra-sthalams.md; cross-link the Muchukunda lineage coverage.

title: Sakshi Gopal — the witness Gopala who walked from Vrindavan
brief: The Krishna image that walked behind a young brahmin as legal witness to a marriage-promise, rooting at the spot where he looked back — a fixed stop on the Puri pilgrimage and a signature Gaudiya story. Source: Chaitanya Charitamrita, Madhya-lila 5; Sakshigopal temple tradition, Odisha. Verified: sakshi-gopal greps return zero; jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md does not treat it.

title: Kumbakonam — Adi Kumbheshwara, the amrita-pot of the pralaya, and the Mahamaham
brief: The name-charter: Brahma's kumbha of creation-seeds drifts on the pralaya flood and grounds here; Shiva the kirata's arrow breaks it, the nectar pooling as the Mahamaham tank — basis of the 12-yearly 'Kumbh of the South' when nine rivers converge. Source: Adi Kumbheshwarar sthala-purana (Skanda tradition); Tevaram-sung Paadal Petra Sthalam. Verified: mahamaham has a single line in kumbh-mela-and-pilgrimage-cycles.md; the sthala legend is absent though Kumbakonam is often name-dropped as a hub.

title: Dakor Ranchhodrai — Bodana and the idol that left Dwarka
brief: Gujarat's most-loved temple legend: the aged devotee Bodana rewarded when Krishna-Ranchhodrai climbs into his bullock-cart and leaves Dwarka (trad. 1156 CE); the pursuing priests weigh the idol against gold and it weighs no more than Gangabai's nose-ring. Source: Dakor mahatmya / Ranchhodji temple tradition. Verified: dwarka-bet-dwarka-saurashtra.md has only the epithet line 'later enshrined at Dakor'; bodana greps return zero — cross-link the Dwarka file.

title: Tuljapur Tulja Bhavani — goddess of the Sāḍe-tīn pithas and Shivaji's sword
brief: Maharashtra's tutelary goddess: Tvarita/Turaja who came 'in haste' to save the sage Anubhuti from the demon Kukur, slayer of Matanga/Mahisha here; head shrine of the Marathi three-and-a-half pitha circuit, with the Bhavani-sword legend of Shivaji. Sources: Tulja-mahatmya (Skanda tradition); Marathi bakhar tradition. Verified: the only corpus mention is a circuit-membership line inside kolhapur-mahalakshmi-karavira.md; anubhuti and the sword legend grep to zero.

title: Tarapith — Vashishtha's Tārā sādhana, the fallen third eye, and Bamakhepa
brief: Bengal's premier living tantric kshetra: Sati's third eye in the local pitha-reckoning; Vashishtha perfecting Tara-worship by vamachara learned from Vishnu-as-Buddha in Mahachina; and the cremation-ground saint Bamakhepa (d. 1911). Sources: Tara Tantra / Brahmayamala tradition (Vashishtha-Mahachina episode); Tarapith pitha tradition, Birbhum. Verified: only name-drops in dasha-mahavidya.md and shakta-and-tantra-lineages.md; Tarapith is absent from the 51-pitha list-file; bamakhepa greps return zero.

title: Gītā-Māhātmya tales — the parables of the eighteen chapters
brief: Shiva narrates to Parvati one deliverance-parable per Gita adhyaya (Susharma reborn as bullock/goat, the brahmana Jada, the goat-sacrifice, courtesan figures). Source: Padma Purana, Uttara-khanda 175–192 (18 chapters). Verified: only a one-line mention in 90-literature-corpus/puranas/padma-purana.md; the bhagavad-gita directory and bhagavad-gita.md contain no mahatmya material (grep confirmed zero).

title: Aśokasundarī, Nahuṣa and the demon Huṇḍa
brief: Padma-unique cycle: Parvati's Kalpavriksha-born daughter abducted by Hunda; the infant Nahusha raised by Vasishtha, storming Mahodaya to kill Hunda (and later Vihunda, with the Kamoda episode) and wedding Ashokasundari. Source: Padma Purana, Bhumi-khanda 102–121. Verified: ashokasundari appears only as two variant one-liners in nahusha.md (which covers only the Indra-throne/serpent arc); hunda/vihunda have zero real hits — cross-link nahusha.md.

Convert the existing bullets to summaries + link; cross-link pururavas-urvashi.md and chandra-soma.md.

title: Pusalar — the temple built in the mind
brief: The poor brahmin of Tirunindravur builds Shiva a complete temple in his mind; Shiva tells Pallava Rajasimha in a dream to postpone the Kailasanathar consecration at Kanchi because he must first attend Pusalar's — the beloved manasa-puja parable. Source: Periya Puranam, Pusalar Nayanar Puranam (no. 58). Verified: zero hits, though kanchipuram-city-of-temples.md and TIMELINE.md already narrate Rajasimha's Kailasanathar without this crowning legend — cross-link them.

title: Vyuṣitāśva and Bhadrā — sons begotten by the dead king
brief: Kunti's precedent-tale to Pandu: the Puru king dies of excess and his widow's lament wins seven sons from the corpse-voice — the argument that a wife may raise offspring for an incapacitated husband. Source: Mahabharata CE 1.112 (Adi Parva, Sambhava; Ganguli Adi CXX–CXXI). Verified: zero hits corpus-wide; kunti.md and 01-adi-parva.md lack it.

title: Jantu — King Somaka sacrifices his only son for a hundred
brief: Lomasha's tirtha-tale: frail Jantu offered in sacrifice so each of the hundred wives bears a son (Jantu reborn eldest); Somaka then insists on sharing his priest's hell. Source: Mahabharata CE 3.127–128 (Aranyaka, Tirthayatra; Ganguli Vana CXXVII–CXXVIII). Verified: only the roster line in 03-vana-parva.md line 71; no telling anywhere.

title: Māṇḍūka-upākhyāna — the frog-princess Suśobhanā and Vāmadeva's horses
brief: Markandeya's tale: Ikshvaku king Parikshit weds the frog-king's daughter on condition he never show her water, with the linked tales of sons Shala/Dala and Vamadeva's Vami horses. Source: Mahabharata CE 3.190 (Markandeyasamasya; Ganguli Vana CXCII). Verified: only the generic one-liner in 03-vana-parva.md; Mandukya-Upanishad hits are false positives.

title: Indradyumna and Akūpāra — is anyone older than Mārkaṇḍeya?
brief: MERGED (Mbh + Skanda Kaumarika duplicate): the royal sage fallen from heaven seeks witnesses of his deeds through ever-older beings — the owl, the crane Nadijangha, the tortoise Akupara — the source of the 'oldest animals' motif. Sources: Mahabharata CE 3.191 (Ganguli Vana ~CXCIX); Skanda Purana, Kaumarika-khanda chs. 7–11. Verified: akupara/nadijangha grep to zero; all corpus Indradyumnas are the Jagannatha/Gajendra kings — disambiguate against jagannath-puri file.

title: Mātali-upākhyāna — the charioteer's quest for a Nāga son-in-law
brief: Matali tours Patala with Narada (a major cosmographical catalogue) seeking a groom for Gunakeshi, chooses the Garuda-doomed naga Sumukha, whom Vishnu/Indra grant long life — humbling Garuda's pride. Source: Mahabharata CE 5.95–103 (Udyoga, Bhagavadyana; Ganguli XCVII–CV). Verified: only a two-line roster entry in mahabharata-minor-episodes.md; cross-link garuda.md and bila-svarga cosmography.

title: Suvarṇaṣṭhīvin — Nārada, Parvata and Sṛñjaya's gold-spitting son
brief: The Sixteen Kings frame-story: Narada and Parvata's mutual curses over Sukumari (Narada's monkey face), the boon-child who excretes gold, his murder by robbers, and Narada's revival. Source: Mahabharata CE 12.30–31 (Shanti, Rajadharma; Ganguli XXX–XXXI); Drona Parva parallel. Verified: shodasarajakiya-sixteen-kings.md has the frame in one bullet with none of this plot; sukumari greps return zero. Cross-link that file and narada.md.

title: Mucukunda and Vaiśravaṇa — kings conquer only through joined brahma-kṣatra
brief: Distinct from the sleeping-Mucukunda tale: here Mucukunda challenges Kubera, is mauled by rakshasas until Vasishtha intervenes, learning that kshatra needs brahman power. Source: Mahabharata CE 12.75 (Shanti, Rajadharma, Mucukundopakhyana; Ganguli ~LXXIV). Verified: muchukunda-and-kalayavana.md contains zero Vaishravana/Kubera material — write as file or section there with disambiguation.

title: Śānti-Parva minor tale cycle — Jāpaka, Cirakārī, Kuṇḍadhara, Ṛṣabha-Tanu, Pūjanī

Source: Mahabharata Shanti Parva, Ganguli sections as per each tale. Extend or model on minor-upakhyanas-catalog.md; cross-link ahalya.md and mokshadharma-dialogues.md.

title: Uñchavṛtti-upākhyāna — the angry brahmin and the Nāga Padmanābha
brief: The Shanti Parva's closing upakhyana: a resentful brahmin seeks the virtuous naga Padmanabha on the Gomati, hears his vision of the Sun's chariot, and is converted to the gleaner's life as highest dharma. Source: Mahabharata CE 12.340–353 (Ganguli Shanti CCCLV–CCCLXV). Verified: corpus unchavritti hits are Mudgala/mongoose only; all padmanabha hits are Vishnu epithets and the Thiruvananthapuram murti.

title: Mātaṅga and Vītahavya — the two Anuśāsana varṇa-change upākhyānas
brief: GROUPED pair (adjacent chapters, opposed morals): Matanga the chandala-born ascetic whom Indra refuses brahminhood as unattainable in one life (13.27–30), against the Haihaya king Vitahavya made a brahmin instantly by Bhrigu's truth-speech after the Kashi wars (13.31). Source: Mahabharata Anushasana Parva; Ganguli XXVII–XXX. Verified: matanga hits are Matangi/dikpala/Hampi false positives; vitahavya only in gotra name-lists (rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md, bhrigu.md); 13-anushasana-parva.md omits both.

title: Sārasvata-upākhyāna — the sage who preserved the Vedas through the famine (with the Vṛddhakumārī tale)
brief: From Balarama's Sarasvati pilgrimage: Sarasvata, son of the river-goddess and Dadhicha, fed through the 12-year drought, re-teaches the Vedas to 60,000 starved rishis; adjoining, the aged virgin ascetic who must marry one night to enter heaven. Source: Mahabharata CE 9.50–51 (Shalya, Baladeva-tirthayatra; Ganguli LI–LII). Verified: 09-shalya-parva.md and mahabharata-tirtha-yatra-fords.md give only the pilgrimage frame and ford names; neither story is told. Cross-link dadhichi.md.

title: Nimi and Vasiṣṭha's mutual curse — the bodiless king and the origin of blinking
brief: Expand the existing two-line bullet (suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md line 47, which already has the curse and Janaka-churning per VP IV.5/Bhagavata IX.13) with the fuller Ramayana telling: Vasishtha's rebirth from the kumbha of Mitra-Varuna via Urvashi, and Nimi placed in all creatures' eyelids — the nimesha/blinking etiology. Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara-kanda sargas 55–57 (Shastri). Verified: the Ramayana version and blinking etiology are absent; 7-uttara-kanda.md never mentions Nimi. Best as an expanded section, not necessarily a new file.

title: Śveta, the corpse-eating king, and Agastya's ornament
brief: Agastya finds the ascetic king Shveta, who won heaven but gave no food-charity, condemned to descend daily and eat his own corpse in the empty Dandaka until Agastya accepts his ornament — the sharpest anna-dana parable of the epic. Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara-kanda sargas 77–78 (Shastri). Verified: all Shveta hits are the Kalpa/Upanishad/dana-upakhyana figures; agastya.md lacks it — write as file or section there.

title: Bharata's conquest of the Gandharvas — founding of Takṣaśilā and Puṣkalāvatī
brief: Yudhajit summons Rama's aid against Shailusha's three crores of Gandharvas on the Sindhu; Bharata annihilates them with the Samvarta weapon and installs Taksha and Pushkala — the epic's charter for Gandhara. Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara-kanda sargas 100–101 (Shastri). Verified: 7-uttara-kanda.md line 83 has only the one-line settlement note; shailusha greps return zero; bharata-shatrughna-and-their-wives.md covers Lavanasura but not this — could be a section there.

title: Māṇḍakarṇi and the Pañcāpsaras lake
brief: Rama hears music from an invisible lake-mansion: Mandakarni, who stood ten thousand years in water, succumbed to the five apsaras Indra sent and lives with them in the hidden palace — the one embedded tirtha-legend of the Aranya-kanda. Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya-kanda sarga 11. Verified: mandakarni/panchapsaras grep to zero; 3-aranya-kanda.md jumps from Sutikshna to Agastya — best as a short file or section there.

title: The Dog's Justice — Rama's court and the mendicant who struck a dog
brief: A wounded dog demands justice in Rama's open court and asks that its striker be made a kulapati — the office that had damned the dog itself to this birth; a beloved animal-justice parable of Rama-rajya. Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara-kanda prakshipta sargas after sarga 59 (GPP vulgate; Baroda CE Appendix I — flag [late text]). Verified: kulapati/dog-justice greps hit only Yudhishthira's dog and Yama's hounds.

title: Makarākṣa, son of Khara — the vengeance duel of the Laṅkā war
brief: Ravana sends Khara's son to avenge Janasthana; Rama destroys him with the Agneya-astra. Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha-kanda sargas 78–79 (vulgate). Verified: makaraksha greps return zero; per the gap analysis this is best written as an added section in 04-deep-dives/ramayana/6-yuddha-kanda.md (which names Dhumraksha through Nikumbha but skips this two-sarga episode), not a standalone file.

title: The Kurukshetra reunion — Krishna, the gopis and Nanda at the solar eclipse
brief: DOWNGRADED: krishna-lila.md now has a one-line bullet (X.82), but the three-chapter episode — Krishna's metaphysical teaching to the gopis, the queens' narratives, the sage-assembly and Vasudeva's yajna, and its Gaudiya Ratha-yatra significance — remains untreated. Source: Bhagavata Purana 10.82–84. Cross-link krishna-lila.md, kurukshetra-dharmakshetra.md (eclipse-snana doctrine) and jagannath-puri (Gaudiya reading).

title: Rantideva's fourfold charity
brief: DOWNGRADED: bhagavata-tales-catalog.md line 118 now tells the story in full summary and itself flags it '[index-only — candidate for own file]'; the promotion file should add the Mahabharata parallels and Chambal aetiology. Sources: Bhagavata 9.21.1–18; Mbh Drona 67, Shanti 29. Cross-link shibi.md and shodasarajakiya-sixteen-kings.md (roster line).

title: The Pracetas, the Rudra-Gītā, and the marriage to Māriṣā
brief: DOWNGRADED: the catalog (line 55) now summarizes the tale and flags it a promotion candidate; the file should give the Rudra-gita content (the text's Shaiva-Vaishnava bridge), the burning of the tree-overgrown earth, Marisha, and Daksha's rebirth. Source: Bhagavata Purana 4.24 (Rudra-gita 4.24.33–79), 4.30–31. Cross-link the-prajapatis.md and prithu-prithvi.md variant lines.

title: Khaṭvāṅga — liberation in a single muhūrta
brief: The Ikshvaku king told he has one muhurta to live who attains liberation within the hour — the kshana-mukti exemplum Shuka cites as precedent for Parikshit's seven days. Source: Bhagavata Purana 9.9.41–49; cf. 2.1.13. Verified: only the catalog stub (flagged promotion candidate at line 173) and a TIMELINE line; the divyastras 'khatvanga' is the skull-staff, not the king — disambiguate.

title: The return of Devakī's six sons (Ṣaḍgarbha)
brief: Krishna and Balarama retrieve from Bali in Sutala the six infants Kamsa slew — the cursed Shadgarbha sons of Marichi — who sip Devaki's milk and ascend liberated, closing the infanticide arc that kamsa-vadha.md opens but never closes. Source: Bhagavata Purana 10.85.27–59; cf. Harivamsha Vishnu Parva 47–48. Verified: shadgarbha/six-sons greps return zero relevant hits (re-confirmed against the updated krishna-lila.md).

title: Nanda seized by Varuṇa — Krishna in Varuṇa-loka and the vision of Vaikuṇṭha
brief: Nanda, bathing before dawn on Ekadashi-Dvadashi, is carried to Varuna-loka; Krishna is worshipped by the sea-god and grants the cowherds the Brahma-hrada vision of Vaikuntha — the quiet counterpart to the Govardhana Indra-defeat. Source: Bhagavata Purana 10.28. Verified: absent from varuna.md and from the updated krishna-lila.md; it falls between govardhana-dharana.md (10.24–27) and rasa-lila.md (10.29).

title: Sudarśana, Śaṅkhacūḍa and Vyomāsura — the later Vraja slayings
brief: Three uncovered post-rasa episodes: the vidyadhara Sudarshana freed from a python's body, the guhyaka Shankhachuda slain (crest-jewel to Balarama — distinct from shankhachuda-tulasi.md), and Vyomasura the sheep-thief crushed at the cave. Source: Bhagavata Purana 10.34 and 10.37.28–33. Verified: keshi-arishta-keshava.md stops at Keshi; vyomasura/guhyaka grep to zero in all Krishna files including updated krishna-lila.md.

title: Yajña-patnī-mokṣaṇa — the wives of the Vedic brāhmaṇas feed Krishna
brief: The ritualists refuse the hungry cowherds; their wives defy them and carry the feast to Krishna, winning his highest praise — a Gaudiya set-piece on devotion over ritual. Source: Bhagavata Purana 10.23. Verified: still only the single one-line bullet in krishna-lila.md line 41 and a placement note in venu-gita.md; expand as file or full section.

title: Sandhyā's tapas and rebirth as Arundhatī (with Kāma's birth and first curse)
brief: Brahma's daughter Sandhya, shamed by Kama's first arrows, immolates herself in Medhatithi's fire under Vasishtha's instruction and is reborn as Arundhati — interlocked with Kama's birth, Brahma's curse that Shiva will burn him, and the Rati marriage. Source: Shiva Purana, Rudra-samhita, Sati-khanda chs. 2–9. Verified: corpus knows Arundhati only as chastity-exemplar (saptarishi.md); no Sandhya story anywhere. Cross-link kamadeva coverage.

title: Padmā and Pippalāda — Dharma tests the sage's young wife
brief: Told by the Saptarshis to Himavan: King Anaranya gives Padma to the aged Pippalada; Dharma disguised as a lustful king tests and is cursed by her, and her chastity restores the sage's youth. Source: Shiva Purana, Rudra-samhita, Parvati-khanda chs. 34–35. Verified: the only Anaranya is the distinct Ramayana curse-file; pippalada hits are the Prashna Upanishad teacher and a Shani line — disambiguate both.

title: The Shivapurana-Mahatmya frame tales — Devarāja, Cañculā and Binduga
brief: The three phala-shruti frames: sinful Devaraja liberated by dying mid-recitation; the adulteress Chanchula's disillusion and salvation; her husband Binduga rescued from pisacha-hood by her recital. Source: Shiva Purana, Shivapurana-mahatmya chs. 2–5. Verified: chanchula/binduga grep to zero; add as a section to the existing puranas/shiva-purana.md profile, which omits the mahatmya.

title: The origin of Vaṭuka (Batuka) Bhairava
brief: The Kotirudra etiology of the child-form Batuka Bhairava, granted as a son-manifestation of Shiva and worshipped pan-India as boy-guardian. Source: Shiva Purana, Kotirudra-samhita ch. 13. Verified: vatuka/batuka grep to zero; shiva-avatars-and-forms.md covers Kala-Bhairava and the Ashta-Bhairavas but not this origin — write as file or section there.

title: The minor demon-slayings of the Yuddha-khaṇḍa — Dundubhinirhrāda, Vidala and Utpala
brief: Shiva slays the devotee-harassing Dundubhinirhrada; Parvati crushes the shape-shifting infiltrators Vidala and Utpala with her play-ball. Source: Shiva Purana, Rudra-samhita, Yuddha-khanda chs. 58–59. Verified: nirhrada greps return zero; vidala/utpala hits are Utpaladeva/iconometry false positives; adjacent Gajasura (ch. 57) is already covered in shiva-avatars-and-forms.md.

title: Kotirudra minor linga legends — Atriśvara, Nandikeśvara, Mahābala
brief: The pre-jyotirlinga sthala legends: Atri-Anasuya's drought-penance producing Atrishvara; the sinful brahmin lady saved posthumously at Nandikeshvara; the outcaste woman's good goal at Mahabala (Gokarna). Source: Shiva Purana, Kotirudra-samhita chs. 3–11. Verified: atrishvara greps return zero; gokarna-mahabaleshwar-atma-linga.md lacks the outcaste-woman tale; atri-anasuya.md lacks the drought episode — cross-link all three.

title: The seven brahmins reborn — the Pitṛkalpa chain of births (Brahmadatta of Kāmpilya)
brief: MERGED (Harivamsha Pitrikalpa + Shiva Purana 'seven hunters' duplicate): the students who ate their guru's cow pass through births as hunters, deer, and cakravaka birds, retaining memory through shraddha-piety, ending as King Brahmadatta and companions — the classic shraddha-karma illustration. Sources: Harivamsha, Harivamsha Parva, Pitrikalpa (vulgate ~21–24; Brodbeck 16–19); Matsya Purana 20–21; Shiva Purana, Uma-samhita chs. 40–42. Verified: seven-brahmins/cakravaka greps return zero; harivamsha.md has one storyless bullet. Cross-link shraddha-and-pitr-rites.md.

title: Nandabhadra the merchant — faith tested at Guptakṣetra
brief: The Kaumarika-khanda's Job-like theodicy: the pious vaishya loses sons and wife, is baited by a heretic (the Pingalika corpse-trick) to abandon dharma, holds firm, and is vindicated by Shiva. Source: Skanda Purana, Maheshvara-khanda, Kaumarika-khanda chs. 45–46. Verified: nandabhadra greps return zero corpus-wide.

title: Vyāsa humbled at Kāśī — the paralysed arm and the ban from the city
brief: Finding no alms, Vyasa raises his arm to curse Kashi; it is paralysed, Shiva/Annapurna feed him, and he is barred from residing in the city except on the eighth and fourteenth tithis — the legend behind Vyasakashi/Ramnagar. Source: Skanda Purana, Kashi-khanda, Uttarardha chs. 95–96. Verified: kashi-varanasi.md covers Annapurna but not this; paralysed-arm greps return nothing. Best as a section in kashi-varanasi.md.

title: Mahākālavana and the release of Brahmā's skull — the Avantya opening cycle
brief: The Avantikshetra-mahatmya's own Brahma-decapitation: the skull-bearing Shiva wanders until the kapala drops and he is freed at Mahakalavana, chartering Ujjain's supreme sanctity. Source: Skanda Purana, Avantya-khanda, Avantikshetra-mahatmya chs. 1–7 (chs. 2, 3, 6). Verified: ujjain-avantika.md has zero skull/kapala content (re-confirmed); kashi-varanasi.md carries only the Kashi Kapalamocana variant — add as section to ujjain-avantika.md.

title: Mahīsāgara-saṃgama / Kumārikā-kṣetra (Cambay) — Arjuna and the crocodile-apsarās, Stambheśvara
brief: The sthala-frame of the 66-chapter Kaumarika-khanda: the Mahi-sea confluence, Arjuna redeeming the five apsaras cursed as crocodiles, Karttikeya installing Stambheshvara (today's 'disappearing temple' of Kavi Kamboi), and the Guptakshetra. Source: Skanda Purana, Kaumarika-khanda chs. 1–3, 33–36, 66. Verified: stambheshvara/mahisagara/khambhat grep only to a Narmada-mouth geography line; arjuna.md lacks the crocodile-apsara episode.

title: Hāṭakeśvara-kṣetra (Vaḍnagar) — the Nāgara-khaṇḍa sthala and Nāgara-brahmin charter
brief: The largest single sthala-purana in the Skanda (279 chapters): the linga risen from Patala-gold, the founding of Camatkarapura/Vadnagar, and the Nagara-brahmin origin charter. Source: Skanda Purana, Nagara-khanda, Hatakeshvara-kshetra-mahatmya (AITM vols. 11–12). Verified: hatakeshvara/vadnagar hits are only the two literature files plus unrelated hataka-gold cosmology lines (bila-svarga, devas-asuras).

title: Ekavīra and Ekāvalī — the origin of the Haihaya dynasty
brief: The DBP's dynastic legend: mare-born Ekavira founds the Haihaya line after rescuing Ekavali from the daitya Kalaketu with the Devi-mantra — ancestry of Kartavirya Arjuna. Source: Devi Bhagavata Purana VI.15–25. Verified: ekavira/ekavali/kalaketu grep to zero relevant hits (the corpus Kalaketu is the Chandimangal hunter); the Haihaya section of suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md lacks the origin tale — write as section there or standalone.

title: The war of Āḍi and Baka — Vasiṣṭha and Viśvāmitra as fighting birds
brief: MERGED (DBP + Markandeya duplicate): after the Harishchandra ordeal the two sages curse each other into an adi and a baka who battle for ten thousand years at Manasa lake until Brahma parts them — the canonical coda to their rivalry. Sources: Markandeya Purana, Canto 9 (Pargiter); Devi Bhagavata VI.12–13. Verified: no crane/heron/baka content in vishwamitra-vasishtha.md or hariscandra.md (all Baka hits are Bakasura); best added as a closing section to hariscandra.md or vishwamitra-vasishtha.md.

title: Prahlāda's battle with Nara-Nārāyaṇa at Badarī
brief: Prahlada challenges the armed ascetics at Badarikashrama and fights for divine years without result until Vishnu reveals their invincibility — the humbling of the greatest asura devotee. Source: Devi Bhagavata Purana IV.8–10; Vamana Purana parallel. Verified: absent from both nara-narayana.md and prahlada-narasimha.md — write as file or section in nara-narayana.md alongside the Dambhodbhava item.

title: Satyavrata the illiterate brahmin and the 'Aiṃ' bīja
brief: The dull brahmin overhears the dying boar's cry 'ai-ai', unknowingly repeats the Sarasvati-bija, and the Goddess makes him a supreme poet — the DBP's showcase of bija-mantra power. Source: Devi Bhagavata Purana III.10–11. Verified: all corpus Satyavratas are the Matsya-Manu or Trishanku figures; the tale is absent. Cross-link mantra-japa-and-murti-puja.md.

title: Gautama's curse on the ungrateful brahmins
brief: The DBP's polemical frame for why brahmins abandon Gayatri/Devi worship: Gautama feeds ten thousand brahmins through the famine, is framed with an illusory cow, and curses them to be averse to the Devi and Vedic rites. Source: Devi Bhagavata Purana XII.8–9. Verified: distinct from the go-hatya/Godavari-descent version now fully told in godavari-gautami-dakshina-ganga.md §II — cross-link and differentiate; gautama-ahalya.md has no famine material.

title: Karandhama, Avīkṣit, Marutta and Dama — the Markandeya's royal cycle
brief: MERGED (Karandhama cycle + Dama-Narishyanta finale, one continuous dynastic narrative): the sigh-born army, Avikshit's svayamvara capture and shame, Marutta's reign and Naga war, and the Purana's grim ending — Dama's rakshasa-vow offering Vapushmat's blood as his father's funeral libation. Source: Markandeya Purana, Cantos ~119–137 (Pargiter CXIX–CXXXVII). Verified: only Marutta's golden-sacrifice bullet exists (shodasarajakiya, ashvamedhika-parva); avikshit/karandhama/narishyanta/vapushmat hits are genealogy name-lists only.

title: The Vaivasvata king-tales of the Markandeya — Rājyavardhana, Nābhāga, Vatsaprī, Khanitra
brief: Four self-contained tales unique to the Markandeya's vamsha block: Rajyavardhana's lonely ten-thousand-year youth; Nabhaga's vaishya bride and accepted caste-fall; Vatsapri slaying Kujrimbha of the yawning-weapon to rescue Sunanda; Khanitra saved when his brothers' abhichara recoils. Source: Markandeya Purana, Cantos ~106–118 (Pargiter). Verified: rajyavardhana/vatsapri/kujrimbha/khanitra/bhalandana grep to zero story content.

title: Markandeya's manvantara-origin legends — Uttama's banished queen, Svarāṣṭra/Tāmasa, Ṛtavāc and Revatī
brief: The origin-stories for Manus 3–5 missing from the corpus's otherwise thorough manvantara files: King Uttama recovering the abducted shrewish wife and finding his own banished queen in the naga world; exiled Svarashtra reborn as Tamasa; Ritavach's curse casting the Revati nakshatra onto Mt. Kumuda, whence the girl Revati mothers Raivata Manu. Source: Markandeya Purana, Cantos 66–76 (Pargiter). Verified: manvantara-03/04/05 files carry only office-holder lists (Raivata has the distinct Kakudmi tale); ritavach/svarashtra grep to zero. Write as sections in the three manvantara files or one shared file.

title: Yama Gītā (Vishnu Purana version) — Yama's charge to spare Vishnu's devotees
brief: Yama instructs his mace-bearing duta to avoid those who take refuge in Vishnu ('I am lord only of the rest') — a short gita famous in Vaishnava liturgy, with Agni and Nrisimha Purana variants. Source: Vishnu Purana III.7; Agni Purana ch. 381; Nrisimha Purana ch. 8. Verified: only a digest line in agni-purana.md and a tally line in lesser-gitas-catalog.md; the corpus keeps many individual gita files (rama-gita.md, shiva-gita.md).

title: Kāttavarāyan Katai — the impaled guardian-god's tale
brief: Kattavarayan, foster-son of Kali, loves and abducts the brahmin maiden Aryamala, is mounted on the impaling stake and apotheosized as a kaval deity of the kazhu-festival cults. Source: Kattavarayacuvami Kataippatal; E. Masilamani-Meyer, The Tale of Kattavarayan (Harrassowitz 2004). Verified: kattavarayan greps return zero.

title: Muchilottu Bhagavathy — the wronged scholar-virgin's apotheosis
brief: The brahmin maiden who defeats male scholars in debate, is slandered and cast out, answers the questions of hunger and desire in her self-immolation, and is reborn from the fire as the Vaniya community's Bhagavathy — among the most performed amma-theyyams of Kannur. Source: Muchilottu Bhagavathy thottam-pattu (North Malabar kavu tradition). Verified: muchilott greps return zero.

title: Kalkuda and Kallurti — the mutilated sculptor of the Karkala Bahubali and his avenging sister
brief: Master sculptor Kalkuda, mutilated by Veera Pandya after raising the Karkala Gommateshwara (1432 CE) so he could never duplicate it; his sister Kallurti burns the palace, and the pair are deified as paired daivas across Tulu Nadu. Source: Kalkuda-Kallurti paddana (Karkala/Venur cycle; B.A. Viveka Rai, Peter Claus collections). Verified: kalkuda/kallurti grep to zero; Bahubali has only a TIMELINE passing line.

title: The Dhangar god-epics — Biroba, Mhaskoba and Dhuloba
brief: The Marathi pastoralist ovi cycles of Biroba the shepherd-god, Mhaskoba (Kal-Bhairava as the buffalo-field god of Vir), and Dhuloba — the pastoral substrate beneath Khandoba per Sontheimer's classic study. Source: Dhangar ovi epics; G.-D. Sontheimer, Biroba, Mhaskoba und Khandoba (1976). Verified: all three names grep to zero (khandoba file matches Dhangar only as a devotee community); add to regional-and-oral-epics.md or standalone.

title: Goa's kuladevata pantheon — Shantadurga, Mangeshi, Ravalnath, Betal, Sateri
brief: MERGED (02-deities pantheon entry + 06-geography kshetra entry): Shantadurga mediating the Shiva-Vishnu war with a serpent in each hand (Kavlem); Shiva as the tiger eliciting 'trahi mam girisha' at Mangeshi; the attendant Ravalnath, Betal/Vetal and anthill-goddess Sateri; plus the 16th-c. idol-flights from Portuguese Goa to Ponda. Sources: Skanda Purana, Sahyadri-khanda (Gomantaka mahatmya); Kavlem and Mangeshi temple traditions; gaonkari village-pantheon lore. Verified: shantadurga/mangesh/ravalnath/sateri all grep to zero — the corpus has no Goan deity or kshetra file at all.

title: Suchindram Sthanumalayan — the Trimurti linga and Indra's expiation
brief: The one linga worshipped as Sthanu-Mala-Ayan (Shiva-Vishnu-Brahma); the site of Indra's purification (suchi) from the Ahalya curse — he performs the night worship still — with the giant Hanuman and the local Atri-Anasuya framing. Source: Sucindrasthala-mahatmya; cf. Ramayana Bala-kanda 48–49. Verified: Suchindram appears only as pitha list-entry and a source URL in devi-kanyakumari.md; sthanumalayan greps return zero; atri-anasuya.md never names the site.

title: Kukke Subrahmanya — Vasuki sheltered from Garuda
brief: Kumara washes his weapons in the Kumaradhara after Taraka-vadha; Vasuki, hiding from Garuda in the Biladwara cave, is granted refuge and merged in worship — charter of Karnataka's premier sarpa-dosha shrine and its Ashlesha-bali rites. Source: Skanda Purana, Sahyadri-khanda (Subrahmanya-kshetra mahatmya); temple tradition, Dakshina Kannada. Verified: kukke greps return zero; the naga files do not treat the kshetra.

title: Kanipakam Varasiddhi Vinayaka — the self-manifest Ganesha in the well
brief: Three disabled brothers strike a bleeding stone while well-digging and are cured; the svayambhu Ganesha sits in the well-water, held to be growing, and serves as divine oath-arbiter. Source: Kanipakam sthala-purana, Chittoor district (temple trad. Kulottunga Chola I). Verified: kanipakam greps return zero; the ashtavinayaka and Ganesha files do not treat it.

title: Thayumanavar of Tiruchirappalli Rockfort — Shiva as the mother-midwife
brief: Shiva takes the flood-stranded mother's form to deliver Ratnavali's child — Tayum-ana-var, 'he who became even the mother' — plus the Ucchi Pillayar legend of Ganesha fleeing Vibhishana after installing Srirangam's Ranganatha. Source: Tiruchirappalli sthala-purana (Tevaram-sung Paadal Petra Sthalam). Verified: thayumanavar/rockfort/ucchi-pillayar grep to zero; srirangam-ranganatha.md exists but lacks the hill sequel — cross-link it.

title: Ambalappuzha Sri Krishna — the chessboard grains and the pālpāyasam
brief: Krishna as a sage wins rice doubled per chessboard square from the Chempakasseri king, commuting the impossible debt into the daily palpayasam served to all; the temple also sheltered the Guruvayur idol during Tipu's 1789 raid. Source: Ambalappuzha temple tradition, Alappuzha. Verified: ambalappuzha/palpayasam grep to zero; the Guruvayur coverage omits the 1789 refuge — cross-link it.

title: Basara Gnana Saraswati — Vyasa's post-war sojourn on the Godavari
brief: After Kurukshetra, Vyasa's three daily handfuls of sand become the murtis of Saraswati, Lakshmi and Kali (Vasara from Vyasapuri); children receive Akshara-abhyasam here — one of India's only two major Saraswati temples. Source: Basara kshetra tradition (claimed Brahmanda Purana warrant), Nirmal district. Verified: basara greps return zero; saraswati and Vyasa files do not treat the kshetra.

title: Yadagirigutta — the five Narasimhas revealed to Yāda-ṛṣi
brief: The sage Yada-rishi, son of Rishyasringa, beholds Narasimha in five forms in the hill cave; the deity remains as Vaidya Narasimha, curing devotees in dreams. Source: Yadagiri kshetra mahatmya (claimed Skanda warrant); Yadadri temple tradition, Telangana. Verified: the only mention is a one-word roster item in prahlada-narasimha.md, while peers Ahobilam and Simhachalam have dedicated files.

title: The folk Hanuman healing shrines — Mehandipur Balaji and Salasar Balaji
brief: North India's two most-thronged folk Hanuman kshetras: the svayambhu Mehandipur Balaji with Pret-raj and Bhairav as his exorcism court, and Salasar's bearded Hanuman ploughed up at Asota (1754 CE) and enshrined per twin dreams. Source: Mehandipur Balaji temple tradition (Dausa) and Salasar Balaji tradition (Churu, Mohandas legend). Verified: both grep to zero; comparable folk shrines (Khatu Shyam, Vaishno Devi) have dedicated files.

title: Shuka Saptati — the seventy tales of the parrot
brief: The wise parrot detains the merchant's wife Prabhavati from adultery for seventy cliff-hanger nights until Madana returns — ancestor of the Persian Tutinama. Source: Shukasaptati (simplicior and ornatior recensions, c. 12th c. or earlier). Verified: shukasaptati/tutinama grep to zero; slot alongside the panchatantra and hitopadesha profiles in the new katha-literature shelf.
